question: What does the half-year convention mean for depreciation?
expected: All property placed in service or disposed of during the year is treated as placed in service or disposed of at the midpoint of the year, so you get a half-year of depreciation in the first year.
answer: The half-year convention means that you deduct a half-year of depreciation for the first year and the last year that you depreciate the property. You deduct a full year of depreciation for any other year during the recovery period. Figure your depreciation deduction for the year you place the property in service by dividing the depreciation for a full year by 2. If you dispose of the property before the end of the recovery period, figure your depreciation deduction for the year of the disposition the same way.
